question: If 8 solid spherical balls, each of radius 10 cm, are melted and recast into a single spherical ball, then what is the radius of the new ball so formed?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume conserved ⇒ n × r³ = R³

8 × 10³ = R³

R³ = 8000 ⇒ R = 20

**∴ Answer = 20 cm**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of spheres = 8

Radius of each sphere = 10 cm

**Formula used:**

Volume of sphere = (4/3)πr³

**Calculation:**

⇒ Total volume of 8 small spheres = 8 × (4/3)π(10³)

⇒ Volume of new sphere = (4/3)πR³

⇒ Equate volumes

⇒ 8 × (4/3)π(10³) = (4/3)πR³

⇒ 8 × 1000 = R³

⇒ R³ = 8000

⇒ R = ∛8000

⇒ R = 20 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 20 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume Conservation

Total volume remains same after melting

Sphere Volume

(4/3)πr³

Cube Root

Used to find radius from volume
